input.prompt: The camera itself is completely locked off and motionless like a tripod photograph, with absolutely no zoom, no push-in, no drift, no pan and no camera movement of any kind for the entire clip. The framed 'NO JAPANESE SAKE, NO LIFE.' pop-art poster on the wall (a hand holding a wooden masu cup) stays perfectly rigid, flat and exactly the same size for the entire clip: its illustration, hand, masu cup, lettering, ALCOHOLIDAY logo, white border and proportions never warp, stretch, resize, shift position or change perspective, as if it truly is a static print and not a generated image. This is a calm still shot of a plain beige wall with the framed poster. The only change in this shot is an extremely subtle, slow and even variation in the soft natural daylight brightness on the plain wall, as if a thin cloud passes far away; the light changes uniformly and smoothly with no shapes, no patterns, no shadows of leaves or trees and no moving shadows. The small red berry tip at the lower left corner stays still. Everything, especially the framed poster, is completely still and motionless. A calm, quiet, relaxed holiday afternoon in a Japanese tatami room with soft even natural light. The sake is cold: no steam, no smoke, no haze. No faces are ever shown. No shadows of leaves or trees, no moving shadow patterns anywhere. All motion is very small, slow and calm.
